senses.definition: To get more of something or make progress.
senses.example: Lena gained speed on the downhill part of the path.

senses.definition: An increase in the amount of something.
senses.example: The tall seedling had a gain of three inches in a week.

senses.definition: An enormous group of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity.
senses.example: Our Sun belongs to the Milky Way galaxy.

senses.definition: A small pouch under the liver that stores some bile.
senses.example: During digestion, the gallbladder releases bile into a tube.

senses.definition: A unit for measuring how much liquid a container holds. In the U.S., a gallon is four quarts.
senses.example: We poured a gallon of water into the cooler.

senses.definition: To run very fast in the way a horse does.
senses.example: The pony galloped across the open field.

senses.definition: A horse’s fastest usual way of running, or a run at that speed.
senses.example: After the gate opened, the horse broke into a gallop.

senses.definition: An activity people play for fun, often with rules and a goal.
senses.example: We played a guessing game while we waited for the bus.

senses.definition: One match or round of a sport or other activity.
senses.example: Our team played its first game on Saturday.

senses.definition: Ready to try something.
senses.example: I’m game if you want to try the taller slide.

senses.definition: An empty space between things.
senses.example: A rabbit squeezed through a gap in the fence.

senses.definition: A difference between amounts or between what people have.
senses.example: The gap between the two runners got smaller on the last lap.

senses.definition: A covered place for keeping vehicles or working on them.
senses.example: We wheeled our bikes into the garage before the storm.

senses.definition: Things you throw away because they are no longer wanted or useful.
senses.example: I took the garbage out before the truck arrived.

senses.definition: A place where people grow plants on purpose.
senses.example: We found the first ripe tomato in the garden.

senses.definition: To grow and care for plants.
senses.example: The neighbors garden in raised boxes behind the school.

senses.definition: A plant whose bulb has small sections with a strong smell and taste used in cooking.
senses.example: Dad crushed a piece of garlic to add to the soup.

senses.definition: A kind of matter that spreads out to fill the space around it. Air is a mixture of several gases.
senses.example: Helium is a gas sometimes used to fill balloons.

senses.definition: In American English, a short name for gasoline, a liquid fuel.
senses.example: We stopped for gas before the long drive.

senses.definition: To take a quick breath with your mouth open, often because of surprise or hard work.
senses.example: Nora gasped when a frog jumped out of the bucket.

senses.definition: A sudden quick breath.
senses.example: The crowd let out a gasp when the ball nearly bounced into the goal.

senses.definition: A door or movable barrier in a fence or wall.
senses.example: Latch the gate so the puppy stays in the yard.

senses.definition: The place at an airport where passengers get on or leave an airplane.
senses.example: We waited at Gate Twelve until our row was called.

senses.definition: To collect things or bring them together.
senses.example: We gathered smooth stones to paint.

senses.definition: To come together in one place.
senses.example: Families gathered around the stage for the school show.

senses.definition: To look at something for a long time.
senses.example: We gazed out the window at the silent snow.

senses.definition: A long, steady look.
senses.example: The kitten followed my gaze to the window.

senses.definition: A toothed wheel that moves another toothed part and can change speed, force or direction.
senses.example: The small gear turned quickly when the big wheel drove it.

senses.definition: A stretch of DNA whose information a cell can use for a particular job.
senses.example: One gene can tell a cell how to make a protein.

senses.definition: A machine that makes electricity, often by spinning wires or magnets.
senses.example: The wind turbine turned a generator that sent electricity to homes.

senses.definition: All the inherited information in a living thing.
senses.example: A plant’s genome contains directions for lots of different jobs.

senses.definition: Careful and kind, or using only a little force.
senses.example: The vet was gentle with the frightened kitten.

senses.definition: Real, rather than a copy or a trick.
senses.example: The shopkeeper showed us a genuine silver coin.

senses.definition: Honestly felt or meant.
senses.example: Jules gave a genuine smile when she saw her friend.

senses.definition: The study of Earth’s places and how people and natural features are spread across them.
senses.example: In geography, we learned why many towns grew near rivers.

senses.definition: A scientist who studies rocks and what they show about a world’s past.
senses.example: The geologist used marks inside the rock to tell how it had formed.

senses.definition: A part of math that studies shapes, sizes, angles, and where things are in space.
senses.example: We used geometry to figure out which pieces fit in the square.

senses.definition: Energy supplied by heat from inside Earth.
senses.example: Warm water brought up from underground can supply geothermal energy.

senses.definition: A tiny living thing or a virus, especially one that can make people, animals, or plants sick.
senses.example: Washing with soap helps remove germs from our hands.

senses.definition: To start growing from a seed or spore.
senses.example: A root appeared as the bean seed began to germinate.

senses.definition: A movement of your hands, face, or body that shows something without words.
senses.example: A thumbs-up gesture told me the microphone worked.

senses.definition: To use a movement to show or tell someone something.
senses.example: Imani gestured toward the empty chair beside her.

senses.definition: To receive, find, or go and bring something.
senses.example: Can you get a clean towel from the shelf?

senses.definition: To become a certain way.
senses.example: The air gets colder after sunset.

senses.definition: To arrive at a place.
senses.example: We got to the station just in time.

senses.definition: To make an idea clear to someone else.
senses.example: Could a drawing help you get across why the bridge bends?

senses.definition: To learn how to do something well enough to keep going on your own.
senses.example: It took a few tries to get the hang of the skateboard.

senses.definition: A hot spring that sometimes shoots water and steam out of the ground.
senses.example: A geyser sent a burst of hot water up into the air.

senses.definition: In some stories and beliefs, the spirit of a person who has died.
senses.example: In the play, a friendly ghost helped the children find the missing key.

senses.definition: A very large person or creature, especially in a story.
senses.example: The giant in the story could step over a house.

senses.definition: Much bigger than usual.
senses.example: We rolled a giant snowball across the yard.

senses.definition: Feeling dizzy or so excited that it is hard to stay calm.
senses.example: We felt giddy with excitement before the curtain opened.

senses.definition: Something you give someone without asking for payment.
senses.example: Mara made a bookmark as a gift for her brother.

senses.definition: An ability someone seems to have naturally.
senses.example: Noah has a gift for remembering faces.

senses.definition: To laugh in short little bursts.
senses.example: We giggled when the puppet’s hat fell over its eyes.

senses.definition: A short, light laugh.
senses.example: A giggle came from behind the curtain.

senses.definition: The firm flap along the side of the head that protects the gills of many fish.
senses.example: A dark mark showed on the edge of the bluegill’s gill cover.

senses.definition: The underground stem of a plant, often used to add a warm, sharp flavor to food.
senses.example: We grated a little ginger into the carrot soup.

senses.definition: A tall African animal with long legs, a very long neck, and a patchy coat.
senses.example: The giraffe reached leaves that the other animals could not reach.

senses.definition: To pass something to someone so they can use it, keep it, or have it for a while.
senses.example: Please give me a turn with the telescope.

senses.definition: To bend, break, or move when pushed or pulled.
senses.example: The branch began to give under the weight of the snow.

senses.definition: To try something and see what happens.
senses.example: I had never sewn a button on, but I agreed to give it a go.

senses.definition: A huge mass of ice that forms on land as layers of snow pile up and squeeze together. It moves slowly under its own weight.
senses.example: In the mountains, a glacier crept down the valley over many years.

senses.definition: Pleased about something or happy to do something.
senses.example: I was glad my friend could come with us.

senses.definition: To look at something quickly.
senses.example: Paz glanced at the clock to see if the bell was about to ring.

senses.definition: A quick look.
senses.example: One glance at the puddles told us it had rained.

senses.definition: Light so bright that it makes it hard to see.
senses.example: The glare on my screen made the words hard to read.

senses.definition: To look at someone in an angry way.
senses.example: Gus glared at his brother for knocking over the tower.

senses.definition: A hard material that often lets you see through it.
senses.example: Morning light came through the glass in the door.

senses.definition: A cup for drinking, usually made of glass.
senses.example: We each drank a glass of water after the race.

senses.definition: A pair of lenses held in a frame and worn over the eyes, in the form “glasses.”
senses.example: I put on my glasses to read the board.

senses.definition: A coating that can become glassy when heated on pottery.
senses.example: The glaze gave the bowl a smooth blue surface.

senses.definition: To move smoothly without obvious bumps or stops.
senses.example: The skater glided across the ice on one foot.

senses.definition: A little bit of light that is weak or unsteady.
senses.example: A glimmer from the far window helped us find the path.

senses.definition: To give off a small amount of light.
senses.example: A light glimmered in the tent across the field.

senses.definition: A view that lasts only a very short time.
senses.example: We caught a glimpse of a deer before it slipped into the trees.

senses.definition: To see something briefly.
senses.example: I glimpsed the school bus through the kitchen window.

senses.definition: To flash with many tiny points of light.
senses.example: The sandy path glittered in the sun.

senses.definition: Very small shiny pieces used to decorate things.
senses.example: Ellie shook silver glitter over the wet glue.

senses.definition: A round model of Earth or another world.
senses.example: I turned the globe until I could see Australia.

senses.definition: A round object or covering shaped like a ball.
senses.example: A glass globe covered the light on the porch.

senses.definition: Dark or dull enough to feel cheerless.
senses.example: The hallway looked gloomy with the lights off.

senses.definition: Feeling sad or expecting things to go badly.
senses.example: Jules felt gloomy when the picnic was canceled.

senses.definition: To give off a steady light or appear bright with warmth or color.
senses.example: The campfire glowed after the flames died down.

senses.definition: A soft, steady light.
senses.example: The lamp cast a warm glow across the wall.

senses.definition: A sticky substance used to hold things together.
senses.example: One drop of glue held the eye on the cardboard frog.

senses.definition: To attach with a sticky substance.
senses.example: Glue the paper roof to the top of the model.

senses.definition: A carved, drawn, or printed sign that represents something, such as a sound, word, or number.
senses.example: The Maya writer used a glyph for a day in the calendar.

senses.definition: To move or travel from one place to another.
senses.example: We went home before the rain started.

senses.definition: To fit, match, or belong somewhere.
senses.example: The blue block goes into the square hole.

senses.definition: To look at or talk through something again to understand or check it.
senses.example: Before we played, the referee helped us go over the rules.

senses.definition: Something you are trying to do or reach.
senses.example: My goal is to read a whole chapter tonight.

senses.definition: The place you try to send a ball or puck to score, or the score when you do.
senses.example: The goalie stood in front of the goal.

senses.definition: An animal with hooves that often has horns and a beard and can climb steep or rocky places.
senses.example: A goat balanced on a log beside the fence.

senses.definition: A game where players use clubs to hit a ball into holes in as few hits as they can.
senses.example: In miniature golf, we had to hit the ball through a tiny windmill.

senses.definition: To play a game of golf.
senses.example: We golfed on a small course outside town.

senses.definition: Having a quality people want or approve of.
senses.example: That was a good plan because everyone got a turn.

senses.definition: Skilled at doing something.
senses.example: Cora is good at drawing maps.

senses.definition: Kind or willing to help.
senses.example: Luz is a good friend who checks on me when I’m upset.

senses.definition: A large waterbird with a long neck and feet that help it paddle.
senses.example: A goose and its young crossed the path near the pond.

senses.definition: Very beautiful or pleasing to look at.
senses.example: A gorgeous pink cloud stretched across the sky.

senses.definition: Talk about other people’s private lives, often without knowing if what is said is true.
senses.example: We changed the subject when the talk turned into gossip.

senses.definition: To talk about other people’s private lives.
senses.example: I told my friends I would rather play a game than gossip about a classmate.

senses.definition: To be in charge of making and carrying out rules for a place or group.
senses.example: The elected council helps govern the town.

senses.definition: To guide or control how something happens.
senses.example: The handbook describes the rules that govern the contest.

senses.definition: To take hold of something quickly.
senses.example: I grabbed my hat as the wind began blowing.

senses.definition: Moving or looking smooth, easy, and pleasing.
senses.example: The dancer made a graceful turn on one foot.

senses.definition: A year or level at school.
senses.example: Next year Asher will be in fourth grade.

senses.definition: A mark a teacher gives for schoolwork.
senses.example: I worked hard to earn a good grade on my report.

senses.definition: To check work and give it a mark.
senses.example: Our teacher will grade the quizzes this afternoon.

senses.definition: To join a piece cut from one plant to a part of another plant so that they grow together.
senses.example: The orchard worker grafted a branch from an apple tree onto another tree’s roots.

senses.definition: A small hard seed or fruit from a crop such as corn, wheat, oats or rice.
senses.example: The cook stirred the grains of rice in the pot.

senses.definition: The patterns a language uses to build words and sentences.
senses.example: Our grammar lesson explained how to make some nouns plural.

senses.definition: Large and impressive, or especially important.
senses.example: A grand staircase curved up both sides of the hall.

senses.definition: The mother or father of one of your parents.
senses.example: My grandparent showed me how to fold the old map.

senses.definition: To officially give someone something they have asked for.
senses.example: The principal granted our request to use the gym.

senses.definition: Money given for a certain purpose, usually without asking for it back.
senses.example: The library used a grant to buy new books.

senses.definition: A large round fruit with a thick skin and juicy, often slightly bitter sections.
senses.example: I shared a pink grapefruit with my aunt at breakfast.

senses.definition: A picture that shows numbers, amounts, or how one thing changes with another.
senses.example: The graph showed how tall the plant grew each week.

senses.definition: To show information in a graph.
senses.example: We graphed the class’s favorite kinds of fruit.

senses.definition: A soft form of carbon in which flat layers of atoms can slip past one another.
senses.example: A pencil point leaves some graphite on the page as it moves.

senses.definition: To take hold of something firmly.
senses.example: Grasp the rail as you walk down the steps.

senses.definition: To understand something.
senses.example: A simple picture helped me grasp the idea.

senses.definition: A kind of plant that usually has narrow leaves, such as the plants that make up a lawn.
senses.example: The rain left the grass wet for hours.

senses.definition: An insect with long back legs that help it jump.
senses.example: A grasshopper sprang out of the tall grass as I passed.

senses.definition: To rub food across a tool with sharp holes or edges so it breaks into small shreds.
senses.example: We grated cheese over the soup.

senses.definition: A frame with bars or openings that lets air, water, or light through.
senses.example: The rain ran through the grate beside the road.

senses.definition: Feeling thankful for something someone did or for something good that happened.
senses.example: I was grateful that my friend saved me a seat.

senses.definition: Small stones often used to cover paths or roads.
senses.example: The wagon wheels crunched over the gravel.

senses.definition: Plant growth that changes direction in response to gravity.
senses.example: Through gravitropism, a root bent downward after the seed changed position.

senses.definition: The attraction between things that have mass. It pulls objects toward Earth and holds planets in their paths around the Sun.
senses.example: Gravity pulls a dropped pencil toward the floor.

senses.definition: A sauce often made from the liquid left after cooking meat or vegetables.
senses.example: I poured gravy over the mashed potatoes.

senses.definition: Between black and white in color, like many clouds before rain.
senses.example: The rabbit had soft gray fur.

senses.definition: The largest positive whole number that divides evenly into each of two or more given positive whole numbers.
senses.example: The greatest common factor of six and 15 is three.

senses.definition: Wanting more than you need and being unwilling to share.
senses.example: The greedy character hid all the cookies so no one else could have one.

senses.definition: Having a color like many plants and leaves.
senses.example: I used a green pencil to draw the grass.

senses.definition: Not ripe yet.
senses.example: The bananas were still green, so we waited a few days.

senses.definition: Leaves or other green vegetables that people eat, usually called “greens.”
senses.example: We added greens to the soup just before it was ready.

senses.definition: A building roof made to support growing plants.
senses.example: The school’s green roof caught some of the rain during the shower.

senses.definition: To welcome someone or say hello.
senses.example: The crossing guard greeted us with a wave.

senses.definition: A pattern of lines that makes rows and columns.
senses.example: I marked a small X in the second row of the grid.

senses.definition: Deep sadness after a loss, especially when someone dies.
senses.example: She felt grief when her old dog died, and drawing pictures of him helped her remember him.

senses.definition: A cooking tool with an open metal surface over or beside a heat source.
senses.example: My uncle cooked corn on the outdoor grill.

senses.definition: To cook on a grill or using direct heat.
senses.example: We grilled peaches until they softened.

senses.definition: Serious, sad, or showing little hope.
senses.example: The players looked grim when their best shot missed.

senses.definition: A wide smile.
senses.example: Grandpa’s grin showed that he liked the surprise.

senses.definition: To smile widely.
senses.example: The children grinned as they pulled the first carrot.

senses.definition: To crush or rub something into smaller bits or a powder.
senses.example: We ground dried leaves into tiny pieces for the artwork.

senses.definition: To rub hard surfaces against each other with a rough sound.
senses.example: Sand made the gears grind when I turned the handle.

senses.definition: A firm hold.
senses.example: I kept a firm grip on the handle while we carried the basket.

senses.definition: To hold something tightly.
senses.example: Amir gripped the rope with both hands.

senses.definition: To make a low sound because something hurts, takes effort, or annoys you.
senses.example: Everyone groaned when it started raining just before recess.

senses.definition: A low sound made with effort, pain, or annoyance.
senses.example: A groan came from under the heavy pile of blankets.

senses.definition: Food and other things you buy for your home, often called “groceries.”
senses.example: We carried the groceries in two canvas bags.

senses.definition: A store that sells food and things people often use at home.
senses.example: The grocery on our block sells fresh bread.

senses.definition: The surface of the land beneath your feet.
senses.example: The acorns fell to the ground.

senses.definition: A place used for a certain activity.
senses.example: We walked across the school grounds to the playing field.

senses.definition: Past form of “grind.” It can mean crushed into smaller pieces by pressing and rubbing.
senses.example: We ground the crackers into crumbs.

senses.definition: Water found below the surface in gaps in soil and rock.
senses.example: Some of the rain soaked down and became groundwater.

senses.definition: People or things gathered or thought of together.
senses.example: A group of students put on the play.

senses.definition: To arrange people or things in sets.
senses.example: Can you group these buttons by color?

senses.definition: To get bigger or develop over time, or to make a plant develop by taking care of it.
senses.example: The bean plants grew taller each week.

senses.definition: To gradually become different.
senses.example: The room grew quiet as the play began.

senses.definition: An adult person.
senses.example: Ask a grown-up to help if the lid is stuck.

senses.definition: Old enough to be an adult or seeming ready for adult duties.
senses.example: In the story, the grown-up children came back to visit their old school.

senses.definition: Easily annoyed or in a bad mood.
senses.example: I got grumpy after waiting in the long line without a snack.

senses.definition: A promise that something will happen, work, or be repaired if it fails.
senses.example: The shop gave us a guarantee that it would fix the clock if it stopped again.

senses.definition: To make a firm promise about what will happen.
senses.example: I can guarantee I will give back your book by Monday.

senses.definition: A person or thing that protects someone or keeps a place safe.
senses.example: A guard checked the doors after the museum closed.

senses.definition: To watch over or protect something.
senses.example: The mother bird stayed near to guard her nest.

senses.definition: To answer without being sure you are right.
senses.example: Can you guess what is inside this box?

senses.definition: An answer you give without knowing whether it is right.
senses.example: My guess was twelve, and the answer was thirteen.

senses.definition: Someone invited to visit, join an event, or stay at a place.
senses.example: A guest from the animal shelter brought a rabbit to our class.

senses.definition: A person or book that helps you find your way or learn about something.
senses.example: Our guide knew which trail led to the waterfall.

senses.definition: To show someone the way or help them choose what to do.
senses.example: The lines on the paper guide me as I write.

senses.definition: To swallow quickly or in big mouthfuls.
senses.example: We gulped water after the long run.

senses.definition: A large swallow.
senses.example: I took a gulp of lemonade and went back to the game.

senses.definition: A room or building where people exercise or play indoor sports.
senses.example: We played basketball in the gym after lunch.

senses.definition: A person who performs exercises that require strength, balance, and control.
senses.example: The gymnast took a deep breath before stepping onto the balance beam.
